input.prompt: The camera itself is completely locked off and motionless like a tripod photograph, with absolutely no zoom, no push-in, no drift, no pan and no camera movement of any kind for the entire clip. The framed 'NO JAPANESE SAKE, NO LIFE.' pop-art poster on the wall (a hand holding a wooden masu cup) stays perfectly rigid, flat and exactly the same size for the entire clip: its illustration, hand, masu cup, lettering, ALCOHOLIDAY logo, white border and proportions never warp, stretch, resize, shift position or change perspective, as if it truly is a static print and not a generated image. The only motion anywhere in this shot is the hand of the person in the navy plaid shirt at the right edge of the table: his resting hand slowly and slightly slides a few centimeters toward the small white sake cup in front of him and his fingertips lightly touch the cup; the cup stays on the table and is not lifted high. His arm, shoulder and body do not rise or move otherwise, and his face never appears. His hand keeps exactly five natural fingers and every sake cup keeps exactly its original small round shape and size. Everything else, including the person in the grey knit sweater in the foreground, the bottles, the tokkuri, all sake cups, all food and dishes, the red berry branch, the cabinet, the shoji screen and the poster, is completely still and motionless. A calm, quiet, relaxed holiday afternoon in a Japanese tatami room with soft even natural light. The sake is cold: no steam, no smoke, no haze. No faces are ever shown. No shadows of leaves or trees, no moving shadow patterns anywhere. All motion is very small, slow and calm.
